contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: payload/filter literal formats: geo point = {lon, lat}; datetime = RFC 3339 string; uuid = uuid string; arrays are same-typed
contract_grounding.note: violates-declaration self-check applied: the observation (200 + status ok on face u1) is an accepted value, so false must be justified as either outside-domain or compliant — it is OUTSIDE THE QUOTED CONSTRAINT'S DOMAIN: the uuid clause ('uuid = uuid string') governs uuid-typed values, and in qdrant payload typing is opt-in per field via payload index creation (PayloadSchemaType::Uuid); the tested field 'uid' had no payload index of any kind (never created in this script run), so it was an untyped JSON string field, and the matching filter {key:'uid', match:{value:'not-a-uuid'}} used the documented keyword string-equality channel (MatchValue::String vs stored Value::String). Neither the doc page nor the source ties uuid literal semantics to a field name. For the uuid clause to bind, the test would need a uuid-indexed field (or a uuid-typed filter face) — the citation as applied to an untyped field does not bind, hence no violation of the assertion as documented. The sibling facts remain recorded for the auditor: ingestion performs no literal-format validation at all (free-JSON storage, byte-equal persist), which the doc explicitly permits.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST POST /collections/{c}/points/payload {points:[1], payload:{uid:'not-a-uuid'}} -> lib/shard/src/operations/payload_ops.rs SetPayload {payload: Payload (arbitrary JSON; only filter has nested validation)} -> segment payload assign, stored byte-equal (no literal-format validation anywhere in the ingestion path) -> later scroll {must:[{key:'uid',match:{value:'not-a-uuid'}}]} -> query_checker::check_field_condition: no field index registered on 'uid' -> fallback branch (query_checker.rs:232-235 'Fallback to regular condition check if there are no indexes for the field') -> ValueChecker for Match -> Match::Value(ValueVariants::String) vs stored Value::String -> stored == val (condition_checker.rs:155-162) -> point 1 matches, control filter (value='6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff') matches point 7. The typed-uuid alternative channel (MapIndex<UuidIntType>, the only place uuid syntax is parsed in the filtering pipeline) was never created on this field by the script; had it been, non-uuid values would be silently skipped on both build (mod.rs:1364-1366 get_value -> None) and query (mod.rs:900-909 -> Ok(None)) sides rather than rejected.
source_grounding.outcome_note: validation_absent is scoped to the faces the chain actually exercised: the ingestion face (payload+set) performs NO literal-format validation of payload values (free-JSON storage), and the unindexed-field match face performs type-blind string equality with no uuid parsing. Where uuid syntax IS validated (MapIndex<UuidIntType>, the opt-in uuid payload index), parse failures are silently skipped, never rejected. No code comment or docstring in the examined files explicitly declares lenient acceptance of malformed uuid literals as intended (the fallback comment at query_checker.rs:233 documents the unindexed-field mechanism, not a decision about malformed literals), so by_design_in_source is not available under the tightened rule — the by-design mitigation ('payload is arbitrary JSON', 'uuid type works the same as keyword') lives in the DOC layer, not in source intent annotations.

mundane_explanation.surviving: by-design-family interpretive defense (not environmental): qdrant payload fields are untyped JSON at ingestion and per-field typing (uuid) is opt-in via payload index creation; the doc explicitly permits storing any JSON and describes string-match semantics, so 'accepted + keyword-matched a non-uuid string in an untyped field' may be read as documented free-JSON/keyword behavior rather than a state-logic violation — this survives for the auditor to weigh against the constraint's literal-format phrasing
